d: Great portico of the royal palace corresponding to the banks of the Euphrates. Throne on one side, to the left of which a lower seat for Tamiri. In the face of the above throne three other seats. Ara in the middle with the simulacrum of Belo deity of the Chaldeans, great bridge practicable with statues, ships on the river, view of tents and Soldiers on the other bank. Semiramide believed Nino with Guards and then Sibari.
Directing room illuminated in time at night. Various beliefs around. Great canteen set in the middle with four seats around and a chair in the face. Sibari, then Ircano with bare sword.
Semiramide, Tamiri, Mirteo, Scitalce, preceded by Ballerini, followed by Paggi, Knights and sayings.
Semiramide, Scitalce, Mirtheus, Ircano and Sibari.
Semiramide, then Scythalce without a sword.

Country on the banks of the Euphrates with ships that are burned, walls of the royal gardens on one side with open gates. Irchano with followers of armed Scythians, part on the ships and part on the bank of the river.
Sibari with bare sword and said.
Mirtheus with bare sword and sayings.
Amphitheatre with gates closed from the sides and throne on one side. Semiramide with Guards and People, Sibari, then Ircano.
